title: Liu Bei Visits Zhuge Liang Three Times
text:
Around 207 Liu Bei was a warlord without a secure base, sheltering under another lord in Jing province in central China. He was in his forties and had spent twenty years fighting and losing. An adviser, Xu Shu, told him about a young scholar living in retirement at Longzhong, Zhuge Liang, and said he was a "sleeping dragon". Liu Bei asked Xu Shu to bring him. Xu Shu answered that such a man could be visited, but not summoned.

So Liu Bei went himself. According to Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms, he went three times before he was received. Zhuge Liang was then about twenty-six.

When they finally met, Zhuge Liang laid out a long-term plan: take Jing and Yi provinces, make alliances with the southern peoples and with Sun Quan in the east, and wait for the right moment to strike north. Liu Bei followed it, and it shaped the founding of the Shu Han kingdom.

Twenty years later, in his famous memorial to Liu Bei's son, Zhuge Liang recalled that the late emperor had not thought him too humble and had come three times to his thatched cottage.
lesson: If you want exceptional people to join you, go to them and keep going. Humility and persistence in asking show what you value.
people: Liu Bei, Zhuge Liang, Xu Shu
source: Chen Shou, Records of the Three Kingdoms (Sanguozhi), Biography of Zhuge Liang; Zhuge Liang, Chu Shi Biao (227)
